key_insight: A simple Monte Carlo, gradient-free random-mutation-and-accept-if-better rule can train deep neural networks surprisingly well, challenging the idea that backpropagation is necessary.
engineering_relevance: This suggests an alternative training path for robust or physically inspired neural systems, especially where gradients are unstable, unavailable, or inconvenient to compute.
method: Keep the mutation only if loss decreases; otherwise retry
Apply directly to deep networks without batch norm or residual connections
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful training on 20+ layer deep networks, wide single-hidden-layer networks up to 16,384 hidden neurons, and a simple Transformer on MNIST and Tiny Shakespeare.
watch_item: The approach may be computationally inefficient due to repeated random trials, so scalability and training time need careful evaluation versus backpropagation.
paper_title: Beyond Backpropagation: Monte Carlo Method Can Train Deep Neural Networks
